assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have transformed frequency metrology and created a practical route to precision at the 10^-18 level.
assessment.attribution: Katori's lattice-clock concept and Ye's decisive experimental development form a clear, complementary attribution.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks now demonstrate exceptional accuracy and stability, with broad scientific and technological use.
uncertainties: The eventual redefinition and application consequences remain partly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Titanium-sapphire femtosecond lasers and robust passive mode locking made ultrafast optical science an accessible experimental capability.
assessment.attribution: The listed contributors represent the gain medium and key mode-locking advances, though this was a broad engineering and physics development.
assessment.maturity: The techniques are long-established and underpin attosecond science, precision spectroscopy, and many laboratory instruments.
uncertainties: Credit for distinct Kerr-lens and semiconductor-saturable-absorber approaches may warrant sharper historical delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The SASE X-ray free-electron laser opened an exceptional new observational instrument for atomic, molecular, and materials dynamics.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical and accelerator-physics contributions of the listed names are central, while large facilities necessarily involved extensive collective work.
assessment.maturity: Operating facilities and a vast experimental program establish reproducibility, performance, and transformative reach.
uncertainties: The division between foundational conception, engineering realization, and facility leadership is difficult to reduce to three people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry made quantum coherence into a powerful instrument for inertial sensing and fundamental tests.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard, and Kasevich are important conceptual and experimental figures, representing distinct strands of the field.
assessment.maturity: Precision gravimetry, navigation-relevant sensing, and equivalence-principle experiments demonstrate sustained experimental maturity.
uncertainties: The field has many essential pioneers and its most definitive fundamental-test outcomes are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light overcame an important quantum-noise limit and materially improved precision interferometry.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the foundational quantum-measurement insight, while Mavalvala and Schnabel represent decisive experimental implementation.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is reproducibly deployed in gravitational-wave observatories and has demonstrated practical quantum enhancement.
uncertainties: The appropriate balance between theoretical originators, optical-source developers, and detector implementations remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction converted electron microscopy into a substantially more powerful quantitative instrument with sub-ångström resolution.
assessment.attribution: Rose's optical theory and the major practical correction schemes associated with Haider and Krivanek give a credible attribution chain.
assessment.maturity: Corrected transmission and scanning transmission microscopes are mature, widely replicated tools central to modern materials research.
uncertainties: The history includes several closely related correction designs and important instrument-building teams.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision model supplied the intelligible physical foundation for high-harmonic generation and attosecond pulse science.
assessment.attribution: Corkum, Lewenstein, and Schafer made defining theoretical contributions, although experiment and theory advanced together.
assessment.maturity: The model has been extensively tested and remains central to an experimentally mature field.
uncertainties: The closely linked experimental breakthroughs have already received major recognition, complicating separation of the theoretical contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision trapping and spectroscopy of antimatter provide unusually direct tests of matter-antimatter symmetry.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse and Hangst are leading figures in complementary trapped-antimatter programs, although the work is collaborative.
assessment.maturity: Antihydrogen trapping and precision measurements are firmly demonstrated and continue to improve.
uncertainties: No experimentally established deviation from fundamental symmetry has yet emerged.
